FSM Global has it all under one roof. But does more choice really make investing easier?

TThink FairPrice or Sheng Siong. When you step into a supermarket, you're greeted by aisles filled with all kinds of products, from household essentials and frozen foods to ready-to-eat meals. What makes supermarkets so convenient is their diversity. With almost everything under one roof, there's something for everyone.

Now, imagine replacing those groceries with financial products such as stocks, bonds, ETFs, unit trusts and managed investment portfolios. That's essentially what FSM Global is, a supermarket for investors.

FSM's History: From Fundsupermart to FSM Global

2000
Fundsupermart

Launched in Singapore as an online supermarket specialising in unit trusts.

What's on the Shelves? Exploring FSM Global's Investment Aisles

With so many products under one roof, FSM Global certainly has its shelves stocked. But just like grocery shopping, not everything on the shelves belongs in your basket. Each investment product serves a different purpose, comes with its own price tag and carries different risks.

What's on the Shelves? Exploring FSM's Investment Aisles

Aisle 1: Stocks — Own Slices of Your Favourite Companies

Without question, this is the most familiar aisle for most people regardless of the investment platform.

Just like choosing your favourite brands at FairPrice, stocks let you own a small piece of companies you know, such as DBS, Apple or Microsoft. When they do well, their share prices may rise, and some pay dividends.

FSM Global offers stocks listed in Singapore, the US, Hong Kong, Malaysia, China and London.

The Price Tag
S$8.80 per SGX trade

Who is it for? Investors who enjoy researching companies, can stomach price swings and usually invest larger sums at a time. But putting too much into a few companies is risky.

Aisle 2: Bonds — Lending Your Money for Income

Not everything in a supermarket needs to be exciting. Pantry staples like rice and canned food won't grab your attention, but they're dependable when you need them.

Bonds play a similar role. They are essentially loans you make to governments or companies. In return, they generally pay interest and promise to repay your money at maturity, subject to the issuer's ability to pay. Bond prices also tend to fall when interest rates rise.

FSM Global offers Singapore T-bills and US Treasuries, alongside corporate bonds from companies like HSBC and Qantas.

The Price Tag
0.10%–0.35% per trade

Government securities: 0.10% per trade. Corporate bonds: 0.20% on Bondsupermart Live or 0.35% standard, plus a 0.10%–0.20% yearly platform fee. The catch: fees and the bid-ask spread come out of your coupon.

Who is it for? Investors seeking regular income or a steadier portfolio, especially those nearing important goals such as funding their children's university education.

Aisle 3: ETFs — Don't Put All Your Eggs in One Basket

Not sure which companies or bonds to invest in? Why not invest in hundreds at once?

Think of the ready-made fruit boxes at FairPrice: instead of picking each fruit, you get a variety in one purchase. Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) work the same way, bundling many stocks or bonds into a single investment. An S&P 500 ETF, for example, spreads your money across about 500 large US companies.

The biggest advantage is diversification: one poor performer won't sink your investment. But when the whole market falls, even a diversified ETF loses value.

The Price Tag
S$3.80 per trade, or 0% via RSP

Flat S$3.80 per SGX trade: cheaper than Moomoo, Tiger and IBKR once a trade passes about S$4,750–6,300.
ETF RSP: from S$50 a month at 0%, until further notice.

Who is it for? Long-term investors who want diversification without picking individual stocks. The ETF RSP suits those investing small amounts every month.

Aisle 4: Unit Trusts — Let the Professionals Do the Shopping

Imagine handing your shopping list to an experienced shopper. That's similar to how unit trusts work.

They pool money from many investors into a fund run by professional managers, who pick investments to meet goals such as income or long-term growth.

FSM Global offers over 2,500 unit trusts, giving investors access to different markets, industries and investment strategies.

The Price Tag
0% sales charge, but not free

No sales, redemption or switching fees. Instead, a yearly platform fee applies on cash and SRS holdings: 0.20% for bond funds, 0.35% for others. CPF is exempt.

Who is it for? Investors who prefer professionals to pick investments for them, rather than researching individual securities.

Aisle 5: Managed Portfolios (MAPS) — Ready-to-Invest Meals

Ever noticed the ready-to-eat section at FairPrice? From roasted honey chicken to freshly prepared sushi, there's something for everyone! The best part? Everything is already prepared, saving you the trouble of buying ingredients and cooking from scratch.

That's how FSM Global's Managed Portfolios (MAPS) work. Instead of spending time researching and selecting individual investments, you can choose from ready-made investment portfolios. FSM's professionals build, monitor and adjust your portfolio on your behalf.

The Price Tag
0.35%–0.50% a year

No sales charge or platform fee. Start from S$500, or S$100 a month. Fund expenses apply on top.

Who is it for? Busy investors and beginners who would rather pay a fee than manage a portfolio themselves. Returns are never guaranteed, even with professionals in charge.

So, What's Going Into Your Investment Basket?

Every aisle has a different price tag. Stocks and ETFs charge you each time you trade, while bonds, unit trusts and MAPS keep charging a small yearly fee for as long as you hold them. So FSM Global isn't always the cheapest store. It depends on what you buy, and how much.

For busy investors, the ETF RSP and MAPS stand out: both let you invest small, regular sums without watching the market. Just remember that MAPS charges a yearly fee, and the RSP's 0% fee isn't guaranteed to last.

Feeling overwhelmed? Just as you'd ask a supermarket staff member for help, FSM Global offers free consultations with its investment advisory team, whether face-to-face, by phone or by email.

Ease of Use: Is FSM Global Beginner-Friendly?

A Supermarket With Too Many Aisles?

Remember walking into a massive supermarket and not knowing where to start? That's somewhat how FSM Global can feel to a beginner.

With stocks, bonds, ETFs, unit trusts and managed portfolios competing for your attention, the platform offers plenty of choices, but navigating them can feel overwhelming.

Unlike more guided investment platforms such as Endowus and Syfe, FSM Global organises much of its website around investment products rather than personal financial goals. While experienced investors may appreciate this flexibility, beginners could struggle to know where to start.

APPLE APP STORE
2.7 / 5
280 ratings
GOOGLE PLAY
2.6 / 5
1.99K reviews

And it's not just us. As of November 2026, FSM Global's mobile app received poor ratings on both Apple's App Store and Google Play, with some users reporting performance issues and difficulties navigating the app.

However, getting started isn't all that difficult. Singaporeans can open an account conveniently using Singpass/MyInfo, while familiar payment methods such as PayNow and FAST make depositing money relatively straightforward.

Research at Your Fingertips

Think of its research section as a collection of shopping guides. Just as you might read product reviews before making an expensive purchase, FSM Global offers market insights, investment research and comparison tools covering stocks, bonds, ETFs and other investments.

These resources are particularly useful for investors who prefer making their own decisions.

However, having information doesn't necessarily mean knowing how to use it. For someone with limited investment knowledge, interpreting financial reports and choosing suitable investments can still be challenging.

FSM Global's biggest strength is also its biggest weakness: choice.

Its extensive investment offerings and research resources make it a powerful platform for experienced investors. However, the sheer number of options and financial information may overwhelm beginners.

Nevertheless, services such as MAPS and free investment consultations provide an alternative for investors who prefer professional guidance.

Risk Management: Is Your Money Safe?

A well-stocked shelf means little if the store isn't safe. Is your money protected, is your account secure, and will FSM Global stop you from taking too much risk?

Mostly, yes.

Your investments sit in a client trust, separate from FSM Global's own money, so creditors can't touch them if it closes. FSM Global is also MAS-licensed. The catch is that your shares are held in iFAST's name, not your CDP account, and aren't SDIC-insured.

Every login needs 2FA: a digital token in the FSM Global app or an SMS OTP. Email OTP was dropped in June 2026 to fight phishing. The gap is that SMS codes can still be phished, and unlike IBKR, FSM Global offers no phishing-resistant passkey login.

Fund risk ratings

Each fund is scored from 0 to 10 based on its holdings and diversification. A 4 is riskier than a 2, but not twice as risky. Think of it as a risk ranking.

Knowledge checks

MAS requires a CKA before buying complex products independently, but the requirement is easy to meet: just six purchases within three years, even through small RSPs.

Meet David Tan, a 47-year-old Singaporean father. By day, David works as a security manager. But when his shift ends, his working day is far from over. He gets behind the wheel as a Grab driver, working late into the night to support his wife, a homemaker, and their 12-year-old twins.

Despite his demanding schedule, David has two important financial goals:

Put Both of his Children through University Saving Enough to Retire Comfortably

David needs something straightforward, affordable and convenient, since he has little time.

How well does FSM Global actually serve someone like him?

The Value of Having Someone to Ask

One feature that stands out immediately is its free investment consultation service. Just like seeking advice from a supermarket employee, David can approach FSM Global's investment advisory team to better understand his options and discuss his financial goals and risk appetite.

Get Investment Advisory Service

Whether you are a new investor, or simply need a second opinion on your current portfolio, feel free to contact our Investment Advisory Team.

Important Note

Online appointments are only available 3 business days in advance. If you need to make an urgent appointment, please call our Client Services hotline at 6557 2853.

Adapted From FSM Global's Website

MAPS: A Better Fit for His Lifestyle?

While FSM Global's self-directed investing features may not be particularly suitable for his lifestyle, Managed Portfolios (MAPS) offer a potentially better alternative.

Rather than researching individual stocks and funds, David can choose a professionally managed investment portfolio that reflects his risk appetite.

Furthermore, his financial goals require different approaches. With his twins approaching university age, he may need to take a more cautious approach towards their education savings. Meanwhile, his longer retirement horizon may allow him to accept more short-term market fluctuations.

RSPs: Investing Shouldn't Add to His Workload

FSM Global's Regular Savings Plans (RSPs) allow investors to contribute a fixed amount automatically each month, including contributions to MAPS starting from S$100.

This could help David develop a consistent investing habit without constantly monitoring market conditions or manually placing orders.

Importantly, the contributions can be adjusted or paused, providing some flexibility when his household expenses or Grab earnings fluctuate.

Is It Worth the Price? Mostly!

FSM Global's MAPS Balanced had the lowest annual management fee among the four services we compared. For David, that's a reason to consider MAPS. He can get professional portfolio management without paying the higher fees in our comparison. See the comparison ↑

Our Verdict: A Supermarket That Doesn't Entirely Fit David

FSM Global's greatest selling point is its variety, yet this is arguably one of the least useful features for someone like him.

Its extensive product selection and self-directed trading tools may require more financial knowledge and time than David can reasonably commit.

However, its investment consultation service, MAPS and RSPs offer a more accessible way for investors to pursue their long-term financial goals.

Two Cracks, Two Fixes, One Busy Investor

David already relies on FSM Global's free consultations, MAPS and RSPs. But two cracks remain, and each of our two upgrades fixes one.

CRACK 1  →  UPGRADE 1: FLEX RSP
His Grab income rises and falls, but his RSP expects the same amount every month.
CRACK 2  →  UPGRADE 2: MAPS AUTOPILOT
His goals have deadlines, but each MAPS portfolio keeps the same risk level year after year.

Upgrade 1: Flex RSP - Investing That Follows His Paycheque

The problem: FSM Global's RSP invests a fixed amount on a fixed date. In a lean Grab month the deduction fails, and in a good month the extra cash just sits idle.

The fix: A S$300 floor after his day-job payday, plus automatic month-end top-ups from Grab cash above a safety buffer that protects his emergency fund. Failed deductions are retried, not skipped.

Why it works: RSPs stay effortless even when his income changes. FSM Global already has the RSP, cash account and deduction systems, so only the rules need to change.

Upgrade 2: MAPS Autopilot - Safer as the Deadline Gets Closer

The problem: The MAPS survey picks David's starting portfolio, but each of the five portfolios then keeps a fixed mix of equities and bonds. Moving to a safer mix as the twins near university is left entirely to David.

The fix: David tags each goal with a deadline once, such as "Twins' university: 2033". Autopilot then steps the portfolio down FSM Global's existing risk ladder as 2033 nears (e.g. Balanced in 2029), with a notification and one-tap opt-out before every move.

The 2032 Stress Test - Why Timing Matters

If stocks fell 20% just before the twins start university, a S$60,000 pot would lose about S$8,400 in Moderately Aggressive, but only about S$1,200 on Autopilot. That could decide whether fees are paid on time.

If stocks fall 20% in 2032 (S$60,000 pot)

Without Autopilot (70% equities)
-S$8,400
With Autopilot (10% equities)
-S$1,200

Simplified: assumes bond values stay flat Show workings

Why it works: It automates the cautious approach David's education money needs, while keeping his retirement savings growth-focused. This "glide path" approach is the idea behind target-date funds. CPF's lifecycle scheme, announced in Budget 2026, will also apply it from 2028.

The trade-off

Less growth in the final years, but for money with a fixed deadline, avoiding a big loss matters more.

Our Final Verdict - Is FSM Global Worth Shopping At?

FEES
Fair, but varies by product
EASE OF USE
Tough for beginners
RISK MANAGEMENT
Safe, with a few gaps
OPTIONS
Huge range of products

Our take: FSM Global is a well-stocked, well-guarded supermarket that suits confident DIY investors best. Beginners like David should start with its consultations, MAPS and RSPs, and with our two upgrades, it could serve busy investors just as well.
